response.reason: Reviewed all ten numbered NL segments against the primary typed plan. The primary plan captures initial entry, endpoints, effects, containment, cardinality, state actions, state retention, and transition groups. The omitted independently violable obligations are event-consumer coverage requirements: NL2 states that the Arrived and obstacle-detected events must be handled 'In the InMotion state' as a whole, and NL4 establishes that InMotion is a composite with three substates. arguments.reason: Cross-view structural contrast reveals a major hierarchy defect: the NL requires InMotion to be a composite containing Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching as substates, but both the PlantUML source and the FCSTM model InMotion as a flat non-composite state with all others as siblings under the root. Additionally, all transition effects required by the NL (SendDeparted, Stop, Send Arrived, Cruise, Decelerate) are absent from the FCSTM because the source embeds them in compound event names rather than declaring them as separate effects. issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL5-INITIAL-ENTRY (binding_hints: owner=InMotion, target=Accelerating). FCSTM: InMotion is_composite=false. Verify facts: initial-entry:transition:line:27 proved (root only). No InMotion-scoped initial entry exists. Source: 'InMotion --> Accelerating' is a regular transition (tr_0006), not an initial pseudostate edge.
issues.expected: Within InMotion (as a composite), the initial substate entered is Accelerating, via an initial pseudostate edge owned by InMotion.
issues.observed: FCSTM: InMotion (state:InMotion:line:13) is not composite (is_composite=false), so it has no initial pseudostate and no nested initial entry edge. The transition InMotion->Accelerating (transition:line:32) is a regular non-event-triggered transition, not an initial entry. Verify facts prove only root initial-entry (transition:line:27).
issues.reason: The contract requires an initial entry edge owned by InMotion targeting Accelerating. InMotion is not composite in the FCSTM, so no such edge can exist. The only initial-entry fact proved by verify is for the root composite (transition:line:27 to DoorsClosing).
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source models InMotion->Accelerating as a regular transition (line 13 in PlantUML, no [*] notation). One could argue the NL's 'begins in the Accelerating substate' is satisfied by the InMotion->Accelerating transition serving as the entry path. However, the contract specifically requires an initial_entry (pseudostate default edge) owned by InMotion, which requires InMotion to be composite.
issues.title: No initial entry within InMotion to Accelerating

issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL5-EFFECT-1 (binding_hints: effect=Cruise). FCSTM transition:line:33: effects=[], triggers=[Reached_Cruising_Cruise]. Source transition tr_0007: event='Reached Cruising/Cruise', action=null.

issues.observed: FCSTM transition:line:33 (Accelerating -> Cruising) has effects=[] and triggers=[Reached_Cruising_Cruise]. The Cruise component is absorbed into the event name rather than declared as a separate effect.
issues.reason: The contract explicitly requires an effect 'Cruise' on the Accelerating->Cruising transition. The FCSTM transition has an empty effects array. Cruise is only embedded in the compound event name Reached_Cruising_Cruise.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source models 'Reached Cruising/Cruise' as a single compound event label; the FCSTM faithfully preserves this. The NL's 'indicated by the signal' language could describe the entire compound label as one event rather than separating Cruise as an effect.
issues.title: Effect Cruise absent from Accelerating to Cruising transition

issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL6-EFFECT-1 (binding_hints: effect=Decelerate). FCSTM transition:line:34: effects=[], triggers=[Approached_Decelerate]. Source transition tr_0008: event='Approached/Decelerate', action=null.

issues.requirement_quote: If the system is in the Accelerating substate and approaches its destination, it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source models 'Approached/Decelerate' as a single compound event label; the FCSTM faithfully preserves this. The NL's 'upon receiving the signal' language could describe the entire compound label as one event trigger.

issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL7-EFFECT-1 (binding_hints: effect=Decelerate). FCSTM transition:line:36: effects=[], triggers=[Approached_Decelerate]. Source transition tr_0010: event='Approached/Decelerate', action=null.

issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL9-EFFECT-1 (binding_hints: state=Approaching, effect=Send). FCSTM: state Approaching { enter abstract Decelerate; } - no effect field. Source: 'Approaching : entry/Decelerate' - no Send signal.
issues.expected: The Approaching state has an effect that sends the 'Send' signal.
issues.observed: FCSTM state Approaching (state:Approaching:line:24) has only 'enter abstract Decelerate'. No effect 'Send' is declared on the state. The source also shows only 'entry/Decelerate' on Approaching with no Send signal.
issues.reason: The contract requires the Approaching state to send a 'Send' signal (effect). The FCSTM state has no effects; it only has an entry action Decelerate. The 'Send' effect is entirely absent from both source and model.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source (PlantUML) does not declare any 'Send' signal on the Approaching state either. The NL requires it but neither source nor model implements it. One could argue 'Send' is an informal label for the state's ongoing activity rather than a formal effect signal.
issues.title: Effect Send absent from Approaching state

issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL9-STATE-ACTION-1 (binding_hints: state=Approaching, phase=do, action='approach the destination'). FCSTM: state Approaching { enter abstract Decelerate; } - only entry, no do. Source: 'Approaching : entry/Decelerate'.
issues.expected: The Approaching state performs a do action representing continuous approach-the-destination activity.
issues.observed: FCSTM state Approaching (state:Approaching:line:24) has only 'enter abstract Decelerate' (an entry action). No do action is declared. The source also shows only 'entry/Decelerate'.
issues.reason: The contract requires a do action 'approach the destination' on the Approaching state. The FCSTM state has only an entry action (Decelerate), no do action. The required continuous activity is not formally declared.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL's 'continues to approach the destination' could be interpreted as describing the state's behavioral nature rather than requiring a formal do-action declaration. The entry action Decelerate partially captures the approach behavior. However, the contract explicitly requires a do-phase action.
issues.title: Do action 'approach the destination' absent from Approaching state

issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-c54615e70e12314cc157 (binding_hints: scope=InMotion, event=Arrived). FCSTM event_consumers: Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived consumer_state_refs=[state:InMotion:line:13]. No consumers in Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching. Source: InMotion->Accelerating (tr_0006), InMotion->Cruising (tr_0009), InMotion->Approaching (tr_0011) are non-event entry paths, not return paths.
issues.expected: The event Arrived must be consumable (have a handler) throughout the InMotion operating scope, including from within its intended substates Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching.
issues.observed: FCSTM event consumer facts: Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived has consumer_state_refs=[state:InMotion:line:13] only. No consumer exists in Accelerating, Cruising, or Approaching. Because InMotion is not composite, the system in Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching is in a different state and cannot process the Arrived event without first returning to InMotion via a non-event transition.
issues.reason: The contract requires Arrived event coverage throughout the InMotion operating scope. The NL establishes InMotion as a composite containing Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching. In the FCSTM, the event is only consumable from the InMotion state itself, not from these states (which are siblings, not children). A system in Accelerating cannot directly process Arrived; it must first take the non-event InMotion->Accelerating path in reverse (which doesn't exist as a direct return).
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: In the FCSTM as-is, InMotion's scope is just InMotion itself (since it's not composite), and the event IS consumed from InMotion. The 'coverage throughout InMotion scope' is technically satisfied for the actual flat scope. The violation depends on the NL's intended composite structure, which is itself the subject of the containment violations (REF-011/012/013).
issues.title: Arrived event not consumable throughout intended InMotion scope

issues.basis: NL4 text; FCSTM inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows InMotion is_composite=false, Accelerating parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034; source inventory shows both at top level with InMotion->Accelerating as external transition tr_0006.
issues.expected: Accelerating is declared as a direct child state within the composite InMotion scope.
issues.observed: In the FCSTM, InMotion (state:InMotion:line:13) has is_composite=false and Accelerating (state:Accelerating:line:18) has parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034 (the root wrapper), making them siblings rather than parent-child.
issues.reason: The NL requires Accelerating to be a substate within InMotion. The FCSTM topology places both as siblings under the root wrapper with no containment relation, violating the structural prerequisite for the intended hierarchical behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The FCSTM may intentionally flatten the hierarchy if the PlantUML source does not use explicit composite state syntax (e.g., no state InMotion { } block). However, the source inventory and canonical IR show InMotion as a flat state with external transitions to Accelerating, confirming the source itself lacks nesting syntax that the NL describes.
issues.title: Accelerating is not contained within InMotion in the flat FCSTM topology

issues.basis: NL4 text; FCSTM inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows Cruising parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034; source transition tr_0009 is InMotion->Cruising (external, not internal entry).
issues.expected: Cruising is declared as a direct child state within the composite InMotion scope.
issues.observed: In the FCSTM, InMotion (state:InMotion:line:13) has is_composite=false and Cruising (state:Cruising:line:21) has parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034 (the root wrapper), making them siblings rather than parent-child.
issues.reason: The NL requires Cruising to be a substate within InMotion. The FCSTM places Cruising as a sibling of InMotion under the root wrapper, with no containment relation.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Same flattening rationale as for Accelerating; the source PlantUML does not use composite state block syntax for InMotion.
issues.title: Cruising is not contained within InMotion in the flat FCSTM topology

issues.basis: NL4 text; FCSTM inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows Approaching parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034; source transition tr_0011 confirms external relationship.
issues.expected: Approaching is declared as a direct child state within the composite InMotion scope.
issues.observed: In the FCSTM, InMotion (state:InMotion:line:13) has is_composite=false and Approaching (state:Approaching:line:24) has parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034 (the root wrapper), making them siblings rather than parent-child.
issues.reason: The NL requires Approaching to be a substate within InMotion. The FCSTM places Approaching as a sibling of InMotion, with transition tr_0011 (InMotion->Approaching) being an external transition rather than an internal entry.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Same flattening rationale; the source PlantUML uses flat state declarations with external transitions from InMotion to Approaching rather than nested composite syntax.
issues.title: Approaching is not contained within InMotion in the flat FCSTM topology

issues.basis: NL2 text; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers shows Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived reachable_consumer_state_refs=[state:InMotion:line:13] only; FCSTM transitions lines 32/35/37 are unconditional exits from InMotion to sibling states; from those siblings, no transition consumes Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived.
issues.expected: The Arrived event must be consumable throughout the InMotion operational scope, including while the system is in any of its substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching), so the train can stop upon arrival at any point during motion.
issues.observed: In the FCSTM, Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived has exactly one reachable consumer: state:InMotion:line:13 via transition:line:29. Once the system transitions from InMotion to Accelerating, Cruising, or Approaching (via the unconditional sibling transitions at lines 32, 35, 37), it is no longer in InMotion and the Arrived event has no consumer. From Accelerating, only Reached_Cruising_Cruise and Approached_Decelerate are consumable; from Cruising, only Approached_Decelerate; from Approaching, only Ready_to_Stop and Destination_Missed.
issues.reason: The derived contract requires Arrived to be consumable throughout the InMotion scope. The flat FCSTM topology means the system must explicitly leave InMotion to enter any motion substate, at which point Arrived becomes unconsumable. This breaks the intended behavior where the train can stop upon arrival regardless of which motion phase it is in.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: In the flat topology, the system could remain in the InMotion state without taking any of the three unconditional transitions to substates, in which case Arrived would be consumable. However, the NL describes the substates as the operational phases within InMotion ('the system operates in three substates'), implying the system is always in one of them during motion, making the InMotion state itself a non-operational abstract scope that the system transitively passes through.
issues.title: Arrived event is not consumable from Accelerating, Cruising, or Approaching due to flat topology

issues.basis: NL1 text; source transition tr_0002 event='Closed/SendDeparted' action=null; FCSTM transition:line:28 triggers=[Closed_SendDeparted] effects=[]; InMotion state has no entry/exit/do actions in FCSTM text.
issues.expected: The transition from DoorsClosing to InMotion performs the effect SendDeparted (per UML trigger/effect syntax in the source label 'Closed/SendDeparted').
issues.observed: The FCSTM transition:line:28 has effects=[] and the target state InMotion has no entry action. The entire 'Closed/SendDeparted' label is encoded as a single event name (Closed_SendDeparted) with no separate effect representation. The behavioral action of sending the departed signal is not modeled.
issues.reason: The NL contract requires a separate effect 'SendDeparted' on this transition. In standard UML transition label syntax (trigger/guard/effect), 'Closed/SendDeparted' denotes trigger=Closed and effect=SendDeparted. The FCSTM collapses both into a single event name with no effect field, failing to represent the behavioral consequence of sending the departure signal.
issues.requirement_quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state and transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source PlantUML encodes 'Closed/SendDeparted' as a single transition label, and the FCSTM faithfully represents this as one composite event name. The 'SendDeparted' component may be considered part of the event identity rather than a separate effect, making the model a faithful representation of the source encoding.
issues.title: Transition DoorsClosing to InMotion lacks the SendDeparted effect

issues.basis: NL2 text; source transition tr_0003 event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' action=null; FCSTM transition:line:29 effects=[]; Stopping state in FCSTM text has no lifecycle actions.
issues.expected: The transition from InMotion to Stopping performs the effect Stop (per UML trigger/effect syntax in source label 'Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived').
issues.observed: The FCSTM transition:line:29 has effects=[] and the target state Stopping has no entry action (declared as 'state Stopping named "Stopping";' with no lifecycle actions). The 'Stop' component of the source label is not represented as a behavioral effect anywhere in the model.
issues.reason: The NL contract requires effect 'Stop' on this transition. The UML source label 'Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' specifies trigger=Arrived and effects=Stop, Send Arrived. The FCSTM has no effect representation for either, and the target state Stopping has no entry action to carry the Stop behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source encodes 'Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' as a single transition label, and the FCSTM represents it as one event name. The Stop action may be considered implicit in the state change to Stopping itself (the state name encodes the behavior).
issues.title: Transition InMotion to Stopping lacks the Stop effect

issues.basis: NL2 text; source transition tr_0003 event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' action=null; FCSTM transition:line:29 effects=[]; Stopping state has no lifecycle actions in FCSTM.
issues.expected: The transition from InMotion to Stopping performs the effect Send Arrived (per UML trigger/effect syntax in source label 'Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived').
issues.observed: The FCSTM transition:line:29 has effects=[] and the target state Stopping has no entry action. The 'Send Arrived' signal emission is not represented anywhere in the model.
issues.reason: The NL contract requires a separate effect 'Send Arrived' on this transition. The UML source label specifies this as an effect component. The FCSTM has no effect representation, and the target state has no entry action to carry this behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Same as Stop effect: the source encodes both effects in the transition label and the FCSTM faithfully uses a single event name; the Send Arrived signal may be considered part of the event identity.
issues.title: Transition InMotion to Stopping lacks the Send Arrived effect

semantic_adjudication.reason: The contract NL-CONTRACT-NL9-STATE-ACTION-1 requires phase=do, action='approach the destination' on the Approaching state. The S4 predicate returned verdict=false: the action is not attached to the do lifecycle slot. The FCSTM state has only 'enter abstract Decelerate' (entry action). The NL explicitly uses the word 'continues' which denotes ongoing/do activity, not a one-time entry action. The alternative reading (that 'continues' is merely descriptive of the state's nature) is defeated by the explicit progressive verb 'continues' in the NL, which is standard language for do-phase activity in state descriptions.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The NL's 'continues to approach the destination' could be interpreted as describing the state's general behavioral nature rather than requiring a formal do-action declaration; the entry action Decelerate partially captures the approach behavior.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The Approaching state must perform a do action representing continuous approach-the-destination activity during the state's duration.
